summary: Bolivia sorts passports into three groups: Group 1 — most of the EU, the UK, the United States, most of the Americas and a number of others — enters visa-free for up to 90 days a year; Group 2 pays for a tourist visa, obtainable on arrival or at a consulate; Group 3 needs a consular visa.

passportValidity.text: Bolivia's Migration Directorate asks for a passport valid for at least 6 months with a tourist visa or stay application. The UK Foreign Office says a British visitor's passport should be valid for at least 6 months after the date of arrival, with at least two blank pages.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.certificate: International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP)
vaccinations.text: The UK Foreign Office says you must have a yellow fever vaccination certificate to enter Bolivia if you are coming from a country listed as a transmission risk. Bolivia's Migration Directorate lists a yellow fever vaccination certificate among the requirements for a tourist stay permit if you will visit high-risk endemic areas.

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel-insurance requirement for Bolivia. The UK Foreign Office says the public health system is overstretched, private clinics in the main cities work with international insurance, and it is very important to have travel insurance and access to funds because you will need to pay up front for treatment.

declarations.name: Customs declaration
declarations.text: Before entering or leaving Bolivia, travelers fill in customs Form 250, a sworn declaration of new goods carried in accompanied baggage (on entry) and of currency (on entry and exit). It is available pre-printed or electronically.

source.name: Aduana Nacional de Bolivia — Declaración de equipaje y divisas (Form. 250)

currencyLimits.text: Currency between USD 10,000 and USD 50,000 must be declared on entry, and between USD 10,000 and USD 20,000 on exit, on Form 250. Larger sums must be moved through a financial institution regulated by ASFI. Customs withholds 30% of undeclared currency, and of any amount above the limits.

source.name: Aduana Nacional de Bolivia — Declaración de equipaje y divisas (Form. 250)

notes: Canada's travel advice says it is illegal to export any item the Bolivian government considers a national treasure (patrimonio cultural) — including pre-Columbian artifacts, historical paintings, colonial-era items, native textiles, flora, fauna and fossils — without written permission from the Ministry of Culture.
Canada's travel advice notes that it is illegal to import coca leaves and related products into Canada.

payments.text: Canada's travel advice says credit and debit cards are not widely accepted outside urban centres and recommends carrying small notes for everyday costs such as street food, taxis and tips. It also says Canadian dollars are hard to exchange, so bring US dollars if you need to exchange cash. The UK government says Bolivia is going through an economic crisis and a dollar shortage.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office advises against all but essential travel to the Chapare region of Cochabamba and says a State of Emergency gives police and armed forces powers to remove roadblocks. It says tourists are at risk of express kidnapping, that thieves impersonate police officers, and that robberies from people taking taxis have increased in Santa Cruz, La Paz and Rurrenabaque; it advises ordering radio taxis by phone.

tips.text: Canada's travel advice says you are at risk of high-altitude illness above 2,500 metres, naming La Paz (3,640 m), Uyuni (3,656 m), Oruro (3,735 m) and Potosí (4,090 m), and that the risk is higher if you ascend quickly or exercise or drink alcohol before acclimatising. High-altitude illness can be fatal.

Canada's travel advice says Canadian dollars are hard to exchange in Bolivia and to bring US dollars if you need to exchange cash. Migration fees are set in UFV and paid into the government's fiscal account at Banco Unión.

The UK government's travel advice says protest groups often block roads without warning, that you should not try to cross blockades, and that recent blockades have caused fuel and fresh-food shortages in some areas. Canada's advice says roadblocks are common throughout the country.
Bolivia's Migration Directorate puts the maximum stay for tourists at 90 calendar days per year.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Bolivia?
faq.answer: It depends on which of Bolivia's three groups your passport falls into. Group 1 — most EU and Schengen states, the UK, the United States, Canada, Japan, South Korea, Israel, Turkey, Russia, Australia, New Zealand and most of Latin America — needs no visa and gets up to 90 days a year. Group 2 pays for a tourist visa that can be issued on arrival or at a consulate. Group 3 needs a consular visa from a Bolivian consulate.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Bolivia?
faq.answer: No. Since Supreme Decree 5497 of 1 December 2025, US passport holders are in Group 1 and no longer need a consular visa or entry authorization to visit Bolivia as tourists — the former USD 160 visa no longer applies. Stays count toward the 90-day annual limit for visa-free visitors.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Bolivia?
faq.answer: Bolivia's Migration Directorate puts the maximum stay for tourists at 90 calendar days per year. The UK Foreign Office says border officials issue 30-day stamps but that you can stay 90 days without any new stamp; Australia's Smartraveller says the stay permitted on entry is 30 days and can be extended to 90. Group 2 tourist-visa holders can apply to the Directorate for up to two further periods of up to 30 days, at 250 UFV each.

faq.question: Can I really get a Bolivian visa on arrival?
faq.answer: Group 2 nationalities can, at land-border and airport migration posts. The Migration Directorate's page that listed the documents, fee and processing time is no longer online, and no official source we could read states them today.

faq.question: What is Group 3?
faq.answer: Group 3 is the list of nationalities that, according to Bolivia's migration authority (DIGEMIG), need a consular visa to enter. No official source we could read states the fee, how long a consulate takes or the permitted stay.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever vaccination for Bolivia?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office says a yellow fever certificate is required to enter Bolivia if you are coming from a country listed as a transmission risk. Bolivia's Migration Directorate also asks for one with a tourist stay permit application if you will visit high-risk endemic areas.
